chunks: Muhammad ibn Bakran al-Naqqash in the Kufa Mosque and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Mokattib in Ray - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani, a servant of the Hashemites, said: From Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, from his father, from Abu Al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever leaves striving for his needs on the Day of Ashura, God will fulfill his needs of this world and the Hereafter.

And whoever makes the Day of Ashura his day of calamity, sorrow, and weeping, God the Exalted will make the Day of Resurrection his day of joy and happiness, and his eyes will be pleased in the Gardens.

And whoever calls the Day of Ashura a day of blessing and hoards something in his house on that day, he will not be blessed in what he hoarded, and he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with Yazid, Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, and Umar ibn Sa'd - may God curse them - to the lowest depth of the Hellfire.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and punishments associated with the Day of Ashura according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* emphasizes the transformative power of intentionality (*niyyah*) on Ashura, framing it as a pivot between worldly gain and eternal destiny. It highlights the Shia practice of distinguishing between mere ritual mourning and active engagement in one's affairs, while warning against treating the day as a mundane occasion of prosperity, which risks spiritual stagnation and association with key figures of the Umayyad oppression.
